text:
The gap between insane model capabilities and somewhat ho-hum real-world consequences of those capabilities continues to interest me. 

The AI prophets seem to have nailed the rate of model improvement but overrated the near-term impact. The unemployment rate is low, financially or infrastructurally devastating cyber attacks seem blessedly rare, etc. 

Maybe we’re in a kind of Engel’s Pause but for real-world consequences, or maybe the better theory is some kind of Messy World Hypothesis where it’s really really hard for new technology to leave its mark, bc the world as it exists is a museum of inertias and frictions.

OpenAI just published 722 maths papers written by a model they haven't released.

372 result families across the whole field. they posed the model around 4,000 open research problems and each result took about 3 hours of thinking compute.

some of what's in there: a zero-free region for the Riemann zeta function, the Hodge Conjecture for CM abelian varieties, the irrationality exponent of π.

the repo ships the proofs in Lean where they have them, so a machine can check the work rather than you taking their word for it. they also released summaries of how the model reasoned on 10 of the results.

their own caveat, in the README: results are at different stages of verification, not everything has a Lean formalization yet, and some of the unformalized ones could have issues.

国庆在家做了个实验：把我做视频时常用的那部分流程拆出来，写成一个简单的视频编辑器。

它只跑在 Mac 上，程序本体压缩后约 2 MB。

这个体积夸张到什么程度，你拿着索尼 A7M4 给三上老师拍一张照片也得 70MB 的大小，接近 35 倍，苹果上最好用的视频剪辑软件 Final Cut Pro  4GB 左右，接近两千多倍的大小。而 FCPX 对我来说，并不比这个 2MB 的软件更好用。

麻雀虽小但五脏俱全, 2D、3D、常用特效、MCP 协议都支持, 甚至支持用 js 来写视频（你并不需要一个 chrome）。顺手移植了前几天风靡的 PDoom  视频。

以渲染 @_mexicat 的 PDoom 为例，我的 M2 Max 64GB的机器上测渲染 4K 60fps，带视频/音频/合成音效 + 各种炫酷的动效，4 个 worker 跑差不多153 帧每秒。（PS: 还有一些特性没有移植过来，但第一版的速度相当吓人）

做完这个实验有个感受：AI 在很长一段时间内恐怕依然取代不了专业程序员，但很多领域专家可能不再需要那么专业、那么通用的软件。

非 AI 时代，专业软件为了照顾所有人的需求，功能做得很全，学习门槛也就跟着上去了，而用户学完才能从这个通用且复杂的软件中总结出适合自己工作流。做视频时 打开 FCPX + Apple Motion , 经常因为这玩意要跳来跳去点点戳戳而学的很疲惫, 而每次剪辑都要做很多 setup，从做内容的角度上说，这部分就纯脏活累活。

我做的是 visual explain 类的视频，核心只有一件事：把问题讲清楚。再适当加一点真人讲解，让视频更值得被信任。这条流程里真正用得上的功能，只是那些大软件里很小的一部分。掌握 AE/FCPX 并不是我的目的，他只是服务于我内容的一个环节。

工具和限制决定了你能表达什么。现在可以反过来：先想清楚自己要表达什么，再让 AI 帮你造一个刚好够用的工具。

刚好够用就是这个时代的 AI 开发底色。

顶级的专业程序员暂时依然稀缺，但"专业而通用"的软件，可能不再是每个人的必选项。

欢迎来到新时代！

The FCC has approved SpaceX to launch and operate up to 15,000 next-generation satellites built for direct-to-phone connectivity

The new system is designed to:

• Target peak speeds of up to 150 Mbps per user
• Connect ordinary cell phones directly from space
• Operate in very low orbit at roughly 326–335 km
• Use T-Mobile spectrum alongside spectrum SpaceX is acquiring from EchoStar
• Deliver orders of magnitude more capacity than the first-generation Starlink Mobile constellation

SpaceX currently has roughly 650 dedicated mobile satellites in orbit

The FCC also granted a waiver giving SpaceX a path to provide satellite wireless service without requiring a spectrum-leasing agreement with a terrestrial mobile operator

Starlink Mobile is moving far beyond basic dead-zone connectivity

India needs @Starlink 🇮🇳

• 11,256 of India’s listed villages still lacked 4G coverage as of May 2026.

• India had 1.093 billion internet subscriptions in March 2026, but only 440.87 million were rural. Rural subscription density was 48.31 per 100 people, compared with 126.80 in urban India.

• BharatNet had laid over 850,000 route-km of fibre and made about 221,000 Gram Panchayats service-ready. However, its Points of Presence were reported operational at only 80,472 Gram Panchayats in June 2026.

• Only 4.26% of India’s internet subscriptions were wired connections in March 2026. Starlink could give underserved communities another route to high-speed broadband.

• Starlink has already built 20 gateway sites in India, according to SpaceX Vice President of Starlink Business Operations Lauren Dreyer, speaking at India Mobile Congress today.

• Starlink says it has developed India-specific security controls designed to keep Indian user data within India.

• Its satellite network could bring high-speed internet to remote villages, mountains and islands where extending fibre or mobile networks is difficult.

• Better connectivity could help rural schools access online learning, clinics offer remote consultations and small businesses reach more customers. Starlink already supports education and healthcare in remote communities internationally.

• Portable Starlink terminals have supported disaster response around the world. They could give Indian emergency teams backup connectivity when floods, earthquakes or storms damage ground networks.

• Direct to Cell could also help ordinary 4G phones connect beyond tower coverage, subject to Indian approvals and mobile operator partnerships.

• The government itself identifies difficult terrain, low commercial viability and infrastructure constraints as reasons for remaining coverage gaps. This is exactly where Starlink could help India reach more people.

• India should complete the remaining clearances and spectrum allocation so Starlink can begin commercial service.

• SpaceX’s Vice President of Starlink Business Operations, Lauren Dreyer, said that Starlink is ready to help achieve Prime Minister Modi’s vision of 100% connectivity across India. She highlighted its potential to connect remote classrooms, support telemedicine and restore connectivity after disasters, adding, “With Starlink, people can get connected within minutes, not years.”

India’s hardest-to-reach communities deserve reliable internet too.
